Title: H9 H3K4me3, ChIP, hypoxia, biol rep1
Characteristics: cell line: H9 | cell type: Human embryonic stem cell | chip antibody: H3K4me3 (Epigentek, A4033) | treatment: hypoxia (1% oxygen, 24 hrs)
Treatment: For hypoxia experiments media was changed to fresh full-serum media and cells were incubated in normoxia (regular incubator) or hypoxia (Biospherix OxyCycler model C42 or ProOx model C21 chambers housed in a regular incubator) at 1% O2 for either 24 (H9 cells) or 48 hrs (T47D).
Growth: T47D cells (ATCC, Manassas, Virginia, USA) were grown in RPMI-1640 Medium (Gibco, Cat#11875093) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (Corning).  Cells were maintained at 37 °C with 5% CO2. H9 hESCs were obtained from WiCell and the use of hESCs was approved by the Stem Cell Oversight Committee of Canada. hESCs were cultured on plates prepared with Corning® Matrigel® hESC-Qualified Matrix (#07181, Stemcell Technologies) and fed daily using pre-warmed mTeSR™1 feeder-free medium supplemented with mTeSR™1 5X Supplement (#85850, Stemcell Technologies). Colony quality, confluence, and spontaneous differentiation was visually monitored daily and differentiated colonies were manually scraped off the plate. hESCs were passaged using StemPro™ EZPassage™ Disposable Stem Cell Passaging Tool (23181010, Thermo Fisher). All cells were maintained at 37°C and 5% CO2 in a humidified environment.
Extraction: Post hypoxia treatment, control and treated cells were washed 2x in PBS and collected (500 rcf for 5 minutes at 4°C) and flash frozen. Prior to each ChIP, antibodies were conjugated overnight at 4°C in ChIP Buffer 1 (25 mM Tris pH 7.5, 5 mM MgCl2, 100 mM KCl, 10% glycerol, 0.1% NP-40, 200 uM PMSF, 50 ug/mL BSA) with 50/50 mix of Dynabeads™ Protein A (Thermo Fisher, 10001D) and Dynabeads™ Protein G (Thermo Fisher, 10003D) at a ratio of 6 ug of antibody to 25 uL of beads per sample. Prior to IP, beads were washed 2x with ChIP Buffer 1 and resuspended in 25 uL of ChIP Buffer 1. Frozen cells were washed twice in Buffer N (15 mM Tris Base, 15 mM NaCl, 60 mM KCl, 8.5% sucrose, 5 mM MgCl2, 1 mM CaCl2, 1 mM DTT, 200 uM PMSF, 1x protease inhibitor, 50 ug/mL BSA), then resuspended in 2x cell pellet volume of Buffer N and lysed for 10 minutes on ice in equivalent volume of 2x Lysis Buffer (1x Buffer N, 0.6% NP-40). Nuclei was pelleted (500 rcf for 5 minutes at 4°C) and resuspended in 6x cell pellet volume of Buffer N, then spun through Sucrose Cushion (15 mM Tris Base, 15 mM NaCl, 60mM KCl, 30% sucrose, 5 mM MgCl2, 1 mM CaCl2, 1 mM DTT, 200 uM PMSF, 1x protease inhibitor, 50 ug/mL BSA) at 500 rcf for 12 minutes at 4°C. Nuclei pellet was resuspended in 2x cell pellet volume of Buffer N. 2 uL of nuclei suspension was diluted with 18 uL of 2 M NaCl in triplicate, vortexed, and sonicated with a water bath sonicator (30x cycle of 30 seconds on, 30 seconds off) prior to measuring the chromatin concentration with NanoDrop Spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher). Concentration of nuclei suspension was then adjusted to 1 ug/uL and separated into 100ug chromatin aliquots. Nuclei suspensions were prewarmed for 2 minutes at 37°C, then 1.52 uL of MNase (Worthington Biochemical Corporation, LS004797) was added for 12 minutes at 37 °C on a ThermoMixer (Eppendorf) set to 900 rpm. Digestion was stopped by adding 1/10 volume of MNase Stop Buffer (100 mM EDTA and 10 mM EGTA) and placing nuclei on ice. 5M NaCl was slowly added to the suspension to a concentration of 0.6 M on the slowest vortex setting to release the chromatin, insoluble nuclei was then pelleted (18,000 rcf, 1 minute, 4 °C), and supernatant was run through hydroxyapatite (HAP) chromatography. 15 uL of soluble chromatin was saved for visualization and the rest of the soluble chromatin was added to 0.07 g of HAP resin (Bio-Rad, #157-0021) rehydrated in HAP Buffer 1 (5 mM NaPO4 pH 7.2, 600 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 200 uM PMSF) and rotated for 10 minutes at 4 °C. HAP mixture was run through Ultrafree-MC Centrifugal Filter (Millipore, UFC30HV25) at 600 rcf for 30 seconds at 4 °C and 15 uL of flow-through was saved for visualization. Then the column was washed 4x with 200uL HAP Buffer 1, 4x with 200 uL HAP Buffer 2 (5 mM NaPO4 pH 7.2, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 200 uM PMSF), and eluted 3x with 100 uL of HAP Elution Buffer (500 mM NaPO4 pH 7.2, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 200 uM PMSF). Flowthrough after each step was saved for visualization. Chromatin concentration was measured again in triplicate with the combined HAP elutions using NanoDrop. Final chromatin concentration was adjusted to 20 ng/uL using ChIP Buffer 1 prior to IP. 15 uL of chromatin was set aside for input control and chromatin was added to beads conjugated with H3K4me3 antibody (Epigentek, A4033). Chromatin and bead mixture was rotated for 10 minutes at 4 °C, washed 2x with ChIP Buffer 2 (25 mM Tris pH 7.5, 5 mM MgCl2, 300 mM KCl, 10% glycerol, 0.1% NP-40, 200 uM PMSF, 50 ug/mL BSA), washed 1x ChIP Buffer 3 (10 mM Tris pH 7.5, 250 mM LiCl, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5% Sodium Deoxycholate, 0.5% NP-40, 200 uM PMSF, 50 ug/mL BSA), and washed 1x with TE buffer, transferring beads to a new tube after each wash step. DNA was finally eluted in 50 uL of ChIP Elution Buffer (50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA, 1% SDS) at 600 rpm for 10 minutes at 55 °C on a ThermoMixer. 35 uL of ChIP Elution Buffer was also added to the input control to bring the final volume to 50 uL. To both input and eluted ChIP DNA, 2 uL of 5 M NaCl, 1uL of 500 mM EDTA, and 1 uL of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K was added and incubated for 2 hours at 55 °C and DNA was purified using MinElute PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen, 28004). DNA as eluted in ultrapure H2O and concentration was measured before and after purification using Qubit dsDNA Quantitation, High Sensitivity (Thermo Fisher, Q32851). Finally, HAP input and elutions were visualized using 2% agarose gel in 1x TBE ran at 140 V for 40 minutes to confirm fragment sizes. | ChIP DNA was sent to the McGill University and Genome Quebec Innovation Center, where it was further validated via Bioanalyzer, followed by shotgun library preparation, and library sequencing via Illumina NovaSeq6000. H3K4me3 ChIP DNA was sequenced to a depth of about 50 million reads and input samples were sequence to a depth of about 150 million reads.
Processing: Raw H3K4me3 fastq files were processed using the nf-core/chipseq pipeline v.1.2.0 (available at https://github.com/nf-core/chipseq). Reads were aligned to GRCh38/hg38 in paired-end mode and all other parameters were kept as default. | The filtered aligned reads were extracted from the BAM files and re-aligned to a custom index of 5’UTR sequences using Bowtie (version 1.2.2) (settings: -v 2 -X 1000 -a). This custom index was created from genomic sequence regions corresponding to RefSeq transcripts with 2,000 bp of genomic sequence added upstream of the annotated TSS, and 10,000 bp added downstream of the TSS. | Bedtools genomeCoverageBed (v2.29.1) was then used to compute the genome coverage of H3K4me3 with -dz and -pc options, and -scale to normalize for library size. The cumulative sum of H3K4me3 coverage was calculated for each genomic region corresponding to RefSeq transcripts, and genomic regions were trimmed at the position where 95% of cumulative H3K4me3 signal had already occurred. | In order to reduce file sizes and computation time, the position (relative to the transcription start site), and the H3K4me3 coverage were collected for every 0.1% increase in the cumulative sum of H3K4me3 signal, such that each genomic region corresponding to RefSeq transcripts would have 1,000 data points summarizing the distribution of the histone mark. | Assembly: GRCh38/hg38 for genomic alignment, and RefSeq rel_109.20201120 for transcript annotations. | Supplementary files format and content: BAM files aligned to modified RefSeq reference described above. | Supplementary files format and content: CDF files (ZZZ tab separated) in the format: RefSeq ID, cumulative sum of H3K4me3 read coverage, positions relative to the transcription start site where the cumulative sum of read coverage increases by 0.1%, and read coverage at these positions, scaled to total library size. This file format was created§ to easily summarize and load large bam files into R, and reduce computation times.

Title: H9 cells, normoxia, polysomal RNA, biol rep 2
Characteristics: cell line: H9 | cell type: Human embryonic stem cell | treatment: normoxia (20% oxygen, 24 hrs)
Treatment: For hypoxia experiments media was changed to fresh full-serum media and cells were incubated in normoxia (regular incubator) or hypoxia (Biospherix OxyCycler model C42 or ProOx model C21 chambers housed in a regular incubator) at 1% O2 for either 24 (H9 cells) or 48 hrs (T47D).
Growth: T47D cells (ATCC, Manassas, Virginia, USA) were grown in RPMI-1640 Medium (Gibco, Cat#11875093) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) (Corning).  Cells were maintained at 37 °C with 5% CO2. H9 hESCs were obtained from WiCell and the use of hESCs was approved by the Stem Cell Oversight Committee of Canada. hESCs were cultured on plates prepared with Corning® Matrigel® hESC-Qualified Matrix (#07181, Stemcell Technologies) and fed daily using pre-warmed mTeSR™1 feeder-free medium supplemented with mTeSR™1 5X Supplement (#85850, Stemcell Technologies). Colony quality, confluence, and spontaneous differentiation was visually monitored daily and differentiated colonies were manually scraped off the plate. hESCs were passaged using StemPro™ EZPassage™ Disposable Stem Cell Passaging Tool (23181010, Thermo Fisher). All cells were maintained at 37°C and 5% CO2 in a humidified environment.
Extraction: Cells (8 x 106 cells per condition) were seeded in 15cm plates 24h prior to the experiment. Media was changed before cells were exposed to normoxia or hypoxia (0.5% O2) for 24h or 48h. Cells were pre-treated with 100 μg/ml cycloheximide for 5 min and scraped in ice-cold, cycloheximide supplemented (100 μg/ml) PBS, using rubber scrapers. Cells were then pelleted in 15 ml conical tubes at 240 × g for 5 min at 4°C, and lysed on ice in 500 μl of hypotonic lysis buffer (5 mM Tris–HCl, pH 7.5, 2.5 mM MgCl2, 1.5 mM KCl, 100 μg/ml cycloheximide, 1 mM DTT, 0.5% Triton, 0.5% sodium deoxycholate) for 15 min. Subsequently, lysates were cleared through a 15 min, 20 817 × g centrifugation at 4°C. Cleared lysates were diluted with hypotonic lysis buffer to set their optical density (OD) at 260 nm to 10–20. Sucrose gradients (5–50%) were generated in polypropylene tubes (Beckman Coulter, 331372, 14 × 89 mm) using a gradient maker (Biocomp Gradient Master 108), according to the manufacturer's instructions. A volume of 500 μl was removed from the top of the sucrose gradient to allow for sample loading. Lysates were then layered over the top of linear sucrose gradients and centrifuged at 4°C for 2 h at 222 228 × g (36 000 rpm) using an ultracentrifuge (Beckman Coulter, Optima XPN-80, rotor SW41Ti), while 10% of the sample was kept for total cytosolic mRNA extraction. Ultracentrifuged samples were fractionated into 2 ml tubes using a density gradient fractionation system (Brandel, BR-188-177), resulting in 12 fractions of 800 μl each. Input samples, as well as sucrose gradient fractions, were mixed with 1000 μl of TRIzol LS reagent (Invitrogen) and kept at −80°C for subsequent RNA isolation. | RNAseq libraries for total and polysome-associated mRNA fractions from T47D, H9, cells cultured under hypoxia (1% O2) and normoxia  (20% O2) were prepared using the Smart-seq2 protocol as previously described83. RNA quantity and quality was assessed by Qubit (Life Technologies) and Bioanalyzer (Agilent Technologies), and 10 ng of RNA was used as input material. After pre-amplification PCR 70 pg of cDNA underwent tagmentation in a total volume of 20 uL using the Nextera XT Kit (Illumina). Sequencing was then performed at the SciLifeLab National Genomics Infrastructure (NGI, Sweden) facility using the NovaSeq6000 (NovaSeq Control Software 1.6.0/RTA v3.4.4) with a 50-base paired-end setup using the ‘NovaSeqStandard’ workflow and S1 flow cell.
Processing: The Bcl to FastQ conversion was performed using bcl2fastq_v2.20.0.422 from the CASAVA software suite. The quality scale used is Sanger / phred33 / Illumina 1.8+. | RNA sequencing read quality was assessed using FastQC v.0.11.8 and MultiQC. | Sequencing adapters and reads mapping to ribosomal RNA were removed using BBDuk from the BBTools suite (http://jgi.doe.gov/data-and-tools/bb-tools/) prior to alignment to hg38 using HISAT2 with default settings. | Reads were summarized using the featureCounts function of the Rsubread R package with default settings and RefSeq gene definitions. | Assembly: GRCh38 | Supplementary files format and content: Matrix of raw gene expression counts based on RefSeq gene definitions.
